title: Chapter 9. On Sleep, Awakening, and the World of the Awake

blocks.text: The teacher said:
"A sleeper can sleep so deeply that nothing can disturb him. Then he dreams, and believes the dream is real.
In his dream, a tiger may chase him, and his heart will pound with fear, as if death itself were truly near.
In his dream, he may see beautiful women playing lovely instruments. Their dance may delight his senses, and it will feel like true happiness.
In his dream, he may be a king or a beggar, a warrior or a monk, a merchant, an animal, a bird, a tree, or a blade of grass. He may be born, and he may die. He may win, and he may lose.
And all of it will feel like the only reality. That is the nature of a dream.
It pulls the mind into an illusion so much like waking life that the sleeper never questions it — he simply believes what he sees.

He doesn't doubt it. He doesn't look for a way out, or try to wake up. He simply lives inside what he sees, and takes it for the only reality. Sometimes he doesn't even remember that another life ever existed.

Our dark world is just the same — a world of sleeping souls. Each one's mind lives inside its own dream, woven from its own nature, karma, and fate. And these dreams weave together whenever we meet one another."
The students asked:
"If the soul exists beyond matter, doesn't that mean it can only wake itself up? No one from outside can wake it. So how can it ever wake up?"
The teacher answered:
"Only a sound can wake a sleeping soul. Not an image, not a thought, not fear, not pleasure.
There is a sound that comes from outside — through the ears, through the mind, through thought and feeling.
A pure, spiritual sound enters the mind and awakens something deep inside the heart. Only this sound can wake the soul!
This is the sound of a mantra. The sound of divine music. It is the sound of a dance the eyes cannot see, but the heart can recognize.
A person doesn't wake up all at once. First, he lives between two states.
He already hears the call, but still sees the dream. He already feels the light, but still moves through the half-dark.
He understands that the world is a dream — but he still cannot wake up."
"Then what should we do?" the students asked. The teacher answered:

"Try to act as someone already awake, even before you're fully awake. Do this through connection with others, through deep meaning, through touching living knowledge and the living hearts of devoted souls. Awakening will come slowly, but it will come.
It may take one lifetime. It may take many.
It doesn't matter. Because even time, inside the dream, is only an illusion.
"One moment, when you blink, can feel like a million years. And a million years can feel like one second. This is the nature of illusion."
Then the students asked this question:
"What lies beyond the dream?"
"Beyond the dark world, where everyone sleeps and each person dreams their own dream, there is a world of those who are awake. A world of awakened beings.
A world where love and light are always present.
There is life there, much like life here. But it is not an illusion — it is real.
There is love there too. But it is pure, free from selfishness or jealousy.
Great liberated souls live there, like Buddhas and saints, living a perfect life.
And there dwells the Supreme Lord, the Source of love.
He reveals himself to each person in the way their heart longs for.
For those who want to love him as a parent, he becomes their child. For friends, he becomes a friend. For lovers, he becomes the beloved.
He dances and sings. He plays and laughs with friends and loved ones, full of joy. He plays like a child, enjoying the games of life.
In his highest form, he wants only one thing: pure love and honesty. Because only then can he give perfect love in return — and only then can a soul receive it.
But the infinite world has other forms too.
Just as our universe seems endless to us, the World of Light truly has no end.
It holds countless forms of being, countless ways the Supreme One appears."
The students asked:
"What can we compare these worlds to?"
The teacher answered:
"To a play. To a theater. In this world, we act out false roles: fathers and mothers, masters and servants, generals and soldiers. And death takes everyone. Both good and bad fade into nothing...

In the Spiritual World, the play exists only for love and truth. There is no death there. Only the setting changes, the picture changes, the scene changes. The game changes — but it stays full of love and joy.
This is where the soul comes from, and this is where it must return.
After playing its part here, letting go of illusion, waking up its awareness, finding love in its heart — the soul returns to that beautiful world.
Home."
